[P3] 哈哈哈 哈！哈！哈！
啊哈哈 啊！哈！哈！
大家笑得好开心呐！
哈哈哈！
白白的牙齿露出来了。
哇哈哈
哇！哈！哈！
咦？
是谁哭了？
大家都在笑，
他为什么哭呢？

[P4] 呜……
呜……
哦，哦，哦！我知道了。
原来是牙齿痛啊！

哇！
有这么多蛀牙，
难怪会牙痛了。

牙齿痛起来，
连大人也会哭呢！

你会不会因为害怕牙痛，
就想，干脆不要牙齿了！

[P5] 你一定喜欢吃各式各样好吃的东西。
要是没有牙齿，
怎么吃这些好吃的东西呢？

把食物放进嘴里，像凿子一样的“门齿”会把食物切断；
像锥子一样的“犬齿”会帮忙撕开食物；
像石臼一样的“臼齿”会把食物磨碎。

门齿
犬齿
臼齿

这些磨碎了的食物，进入肚子会变成什么呢？

[P6] {
  "raw_extracted_text": "磨碎了的食物,进入肚子就变成 营养。

如果没有牙齿
把食物切断、撕开、磨碎,
再好吃的东西也不会变成营养。



















































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































































[P7] 吃过东西以后，
会有一些细小的食物渣渣，
留在牙齿的缝里。

细菌拿这些渣渣当食物，
就会越繁殖越多了。
细菌会制造一种叫“酸”的东西。
“酸”能腐蚀坚硬的牙齿。

所以，食物的残渣要是留在牙缝里，
坚硬的牙齿就会一点一点地被腐蚀。
如果我们不注意，
牙齿就会出现一个一个小洞洞。
有了洞洞的牙齿，就是蛀牙。

怎样才能预防蛀牙呢？

[P8] 刷牙！
对了！要把留在牙缝里的
食物残渣清除干净，
就需要刷牙。

你是不是每天都刷牙呢？

有人说：‘我天天刷牙，
还是有蛀牙呀！’

为什么天天刷牙，
还会蛀牙呢？

[P9] 你喜欢吃糖果、蛋糕吧？
也喜欢喝汽水、嚼口香糖吧？
这些东西里，
含有很多糖分，
糖在嘴巴里
就会变成酸。
这些酸一样会把牙齿腐蚀，
形成一个个小洞洞。
所以常常吃甜的东西，
很容易会有蛀牙。
这么说，要是天天刷牙，
不吃太多的甜食，
就会有健康的牙齿啦！

[P10] 牙齿是我们身体的一部分，
也需要食物中的营养。

吃东西的时候，
如果偏食，
就长不出好的牙齿。
不好的牙齿，
很容易被蛀坏。

吃各式各样有营养的食物，
常常在阳光下
在新鲜的空气里运动、锻炼，
才会有强壮的身体
和健康的牙齿。

如果你的牙齿
都很健康——

[P11] 你才能好好地用力咀嚼食物。
用门齿、犬齿、臼齿把食物咬断、撕开、磨碎，
食物进入肚子后，我们就可以得到营养。

有了良好的营养，
身体才会越来越健康。

如果你的牙齿坏了，或是有了蛀牙，
你就没办法用力咀嚼食物，
身体也就不容易得到营养。

营养不良，身体就会瘦弱，容易生病。
这样你还会快乐吗？

请对着镜子看一看，
你的牙齿
都很健康吗？
排列得很整齐吗？

[P12] 我们小时候长的牙齿叫乳牙，
在六七岁时会一颗一颗掉落，再长出新的恒牙。
每个人都只有一次换恒牙的机会。

在换牙以前，如果乳齿蛀了、碰坏了或是缺牙，
再长出来的恒牙就会歪曲、倾斜、不整齐。

我们没有整齐的牙齿，不能好好地
咀嚼食物，就得不到充分的营养。

我们没有整齐的牙齿，也不能好好地
唱歌、说话，就会变成不快乐的人。

所以不管对大人或小孩来说，
我们现在嘴巴里的牙齿都是很重要的。

你知道你有几颗牙齿吗？

[P13] 请你对着镜子，张开嘴巴数数看吧！
齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 ……
上面和下面都排列起来：
齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 ……
齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 ……
小孩子有 20 颗牙齿，排列起来是这样的：
齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿
齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿
大人有 32 颗牙齿，排列起来是这样的：
齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿
齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿 齿
好了，“牙齿的故事”说完了。
小朋友，如果你有
健康的牙齿，
就张大嘴巴，
露出牙齿，
和我们一起笑吧！
哈！哈！哈！

[P14] 作者介绍
加古里子
加古里子，日本福井县人，一九二六年生。东京
大学工学博士。他对于物理、化学及生物学，心
有无限得心力的执情，图画书和纸板书的创
作。他是著名的儿科科学图画书写作。加古里子
虽然是以一个科学家的身份，参与儿童图画书
的创作，但总是并不希望家长和科学图书作者
作课本，这得反到摊加孩子负担，他说：“图画书
是决不知不教中，一点一滴的引发孩子的兴趣，
让孩子主动去亲近自然，接触人类世代口耳传
下来的科技文明，绝对不可‘强之过急’”。

为了给孩子更好的书，也在创作之前一定经
过缜密的资料搜集，再以再通过考验，充实的绘
画技巧，呈现在孩子面前，所以他的图画书一直
受着家长和小朋友的喜爱。

加古里子的著作很多，除本图画书外，尚有
的著作《你的手》、《我的手》、《牙齿的故事》、
《台风》、《地球》、《海》和《宇宙》等书。

[P3] Hahaha! Ha! Ha! Ha!
Ahaha! Ah! Ha! Ha!
Everyone is laughing so happily!
Hahaha!
White teeth are showing!
Wahaha
Wa! Ha! Ha!
Hmm?
Who is crying?
Everyone is laughing,
why is he crying?

[P4] Wah...
Wah...
Oh, oh, oh! I get it now.
It's toothache!

Wow!
So many cavities,
no wonder it hurts.

Toothache can be so bad,
even grown-ups cry!

Would you, because you're afraid of toothache,
think, 'Maybe I should just not have teeth at all!'

[P5] You must love eating all kinds of delicious food.
What would you do if you didn't have teeth?
How could you eat all these tasty things?

Put food in your mouth. The 'incisors,' like chisels, cut the food;
the 'canines,' like cones, help tear the food;
the 'molars,' like mortars, grind the food.

Incisors
Canines
Molars

What will these ground-up foods become once they enter your stomach?

[P7] After eating, 
there will be tiny food particles 
left in the gaps between teeth.

Bacteria use these particles as food, 
and multiply more and more. 
Bacteria produce a substance called "acid". 
"Acid" can corrode hard teeth.

Therefore, if food residue stays in the tooth gaps, 
the hard teeth will be gradually corroded. 
If we don't pay attention, 
tiny holes will appear in the teeth. 
Teeth with holes are called cavities.

How can we prevent cavities?

[P8] Brush your teeth!
Right! To clean the food particles left in your teeth,
you need to brush your teeth.

Do you brush your teeth every day?

Someone says: 'I brush my teeth every day,
yet I still get cavities!'

Why do I still get cavities even if I brush every day?

[P9] Do you like eating candies and cakes?
Do you also like drinking soda and chewing gum?
These things contain a lot of sugar,
and sugar in your mouth
turns into acid.
This acid will corrode your teeth,
forming tiny holes.
So, if you often eat sweet things,
you're very likely to get cavities.
That said, if you brush your teeth every day
and don't eat too many sweets,
you'll have healthy teeth!

[P10] Teeth are a part of our body,
and they also need nutrients from food.

When eating,
if you are picky,
you won't grow good teeth.
Bad teeth
are very easy to be decayed.

Eat a variety of nutritious foods,
often in the sunlight,
in fresh air, exercising and training,
so you can have a strong body
and healthy teeth.

If your teeth
are all healthy—

[P11] You can only chew food well with force.
Use incisors, canines, and molars to bite, tear, and grind food.
After food enters your stomach, we can get nutrition.

With good nutrition,
your body will become healthier and healthier.

If your teeth are broken or you have cavities,
you won't be able to chew food with force,
and your body will have difficulty getting nutrition.

Poor nutrition makes your body weak and prone to illness.
Would you still be happy?

Look in the mirror,
are your teeth
all healthy?
Are they neatly aligned?

[P12] The teeth we grow when we are young are called baby teeth.
They fall out one by one when we are six or seven years old, and new permanent teeth grow in.
Everyone only gets one chance to grow permanent teeth.

Before the permanent teeth come in, if baby teeth are decayed, damaged, or missing,
the permanent teeth that grow in later may become crooked, tilted, or uneven.

If we don’t have straight teeth, we can’t chew food well,
and we won’t get enough nutrition.

If we don’t have straight teeth, we also can’t sing or speak properly,
and we might become unhappy people.

So, whether for adults or children,
the teeth in our mouths right now are very important.

Do you know how many teeth you have?

[P13] Please look in the mirror, open your mouth, and count them!
Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth ……
Arranged on top and bottom:
Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth ……
Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth ……
Children have 20 teeth, arranged like this:
Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth
Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth
Adults have 32 teeth, arranged like this:
Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth
Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth Tooth
Well, the "Story of Teeth" is finished.
Little friend, if you have
healthy teeth,
open your mouth wide,
show your teeth,
and laugh with us!
Ha! Ha! Ha!

[P14] Author Introduction
Satoshi Kako
Satoshi Kako, born in 1926 in Fukui Prefecture, Japan. Doctor of Engineering from the University of Tokyo. He has an infinite passion for physics, chemistry, and biology, and is known for creating picture books and board books. He is a renowned author of children's science picture books. Although Kako approaches children's picture books from a scientist's perspective, he never wants parents or science book authors to treat them as textbooks, as this would add unnecessary burden to children. He said: "Picture books should not teach directly, but rather gradually spark children's interest, allowing them to actively approach nature and engage with the scientific civilization passed down through generations, absolutely avoiding 'forcing things too quickly.'"

To provide better books for children, he always conducts thorough research before creating, and then tests and refines his illustrations with rich techniques, presenting them to children. Therefore, his picture books have always been loved by parents and children alike.

Satoshi Kako has many works. Besides this picture book, he has also written "Your Hands," "My Hands," "The Story of Your Teeth," "Typhoon," "Earth," "Sea," and "Universe," among others.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《牙齿的故事》的封面及封底，封面上有两个孩子指着自己的牙齿微笑，封底展示了大人和小孩牙齿的结构图，并标注了门齿、犬齿、臼齿等名称，同时包含出版社信息和阅读建议。
[P2] 本页为绘本《牙齿的故事》的扉页，显示书名、作者加古里子及出版社信息，配图有五个微笑的孩子头像和一个牙刷杯子。
[P3] 本页描绘了孩子们在展示牙齿时开心大笑的场景，而一个男孩却在哭泣，引发其他孩子和读者的疑问。
[P4] 本页描绘了一个男孩因牙痛在牙医诊所哭泣，牙医检查后发现他有很多蛀牙，旁边的文字解释了牙痛的原因，并引发读者对牙痛的共情与思考。
[P5] 本页通过图文结合的方式，介绍了牙齿的三种主要类型（门齿、犬齿、臼齿）及其在咀嚼食物中的不同功能，并以提问引导读者思考食物进入肚子后的变化。
[P7] 本页通过图文解释了蛀牙的形成过程：食物残渣留在牙缝中，细菌以此为食并产生酸，酸腐蚀牙齿导致出现小洞，即蛀牙，并以提问引出预防方法。
[P8] 本页通过对话形式，展示了一个女孩提醒刷牙的重要性，同时一个男孩提出疑问，即使天天刷牙为何仍会蛀牙，引发对蛀牙预防的进一步思考。
[P9] 本页通过图文解释了糖分在口腔中转化为酸，进而腐蚀牙齿形成蛀牙的过程，并提出通过天天刷牙和少吃甜食来保持牙齿健康的建议。
[P10] 本页通过图文说明牙齿需要营养，偏食会导致牙齿不好并容易蛀坏，同时强调通过均衡饮食和运动才能拥有强壮身体和健康牙齿。
[P11] 本页通过对比健康牙齿和蛀牙带来的不同结果，强调了牙齿健康对营养吸收和身体强壮的重要性，并引导孩子自检牙齿状况。
[P12] 本页通过图文说明乳牙与恒牙的更换过程，强调乳牙健康对恒牙排列的重要性，并指出牙齿不整齐会影响咀嚼、营养吸收及说话唱歌，从而影响情绪和生活质量，最后以提问引导孩子关注自身牙齿数量。
[P13] 本页通过图文展示儿童和成人牙齿的数量及排列方式，并以对话形式鼓励孩子检查牙齿健康，最后以愉快的语气结束‘牙齿的故事’。
[P14] 本页为绘本《牙齿的故事》的版权页和作者介绍，包含作者加古里子的生平、创作理念、主要作品列表、出版信息、ISBN及阅读年龄建议等内容。
